title: Blob Storage from C#
description: Upload, download, list, and delete blobs using the Azure.Storage.Blobs NuGet package.

data.text: Azure Blob Storage is ideal for user uploads, report files, and static assets. The `Azure.Storage.Blobs` package provides high-level and granular clients for every blob operation.

items: **Append blobs** — logs or streams where appending is common
**Page blobs** — random-access disk images, used by Azure VMs

data.title: Upload and download a blob
data.content: Use BlobContainerClient and BlobClient for common operations.

data.title: List and delete blobs in a container
data.content: Paginate through blobs and remove old files.

data.text: A Shared Access Signature lets you give a client time-limited access to a single blob without exposing your account key.

data.title: Generate a blob SAS URI in C#
data.content: Use `BlobSasBuilder` to create a scoped download link.

data.title: Build a file upload endpoint
data.description: Create an API endpoint that accepts an IFormFile and stores it in Blob Storage.
steps: Create a new controller action accepting `IFormFile`
Instantiate `BlobContainerClient` inside the action or through DI
Upload the file to the `uploads` container
Return the blob name or SAS URI to the caller
data.expectedOutcome: The uploaded file appears in the Blob Storage container and can be downloaded by URL.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `BlobServiceClient` for account-wide operations and `BlobContainerClient` for per-container work
Always use async APIs for upload and download
Use SAS URIs when clients need temporary direct access
Store container names and blob names as constants or configuration
data.takeaway: Blob Storage turns your ASP.NET Core app into a file management system without any server-side disk management.
